title: Generative AI and on-chip synthesis produce new LXR agonists
summary: A recurrent neural network generated de novo LXR agonist designs, and 25 were synthesized in a microfluidic flow system. In vitro screening found 17 hits (68%), and 12 were confirmed as potent LXR agonists after batch resynthesis. Validation is in vitro only, with no in vivo testing, and the sources disagree on the number of designs retained for synthesis.
ai_technology: LSTM recurrent neural network generator with transfer learning, coupled to on-chip flow synthesis

evidence.tested: 25 synthesized designs were screened in reporter gene assays (17 hits); 12 were confirmed as LXR agonists after batch resynthesis, with EC50 0.18 to 4.5 micromolar for LXR-alpha. No in vivo testing was reported.
evidence.unknown: Chemical space was limited to one-step reactions, the primary screen used crude mixtures, two compounds were not confirmed, and the authors describe the work as proof-of-concept.
evidence.ai_role: A generative LSTM pretrained on 656,070 compounds and fine-tuned on 40 known LXR-alpha agonists, with a virtual reaction filter of 17 reaction schemes.
